site.name: Azores Plateau and the Mid-Atlantic Ridge

centre.how: Wikidata Q25263 (Azores) property P625, as used in data/hypotheses.json. Middle of the island group, not of the ridge.

claimed.line: Donnelly (1882): Atlantis was a drowned mid-Atlantic land, and the Azores are its mountain peaks.
claimed.evidence: suppose we found that the Azores were the mountain peaks of this drowned island

found.line: Drill cores and dating show volcanic sea floor 0 to 37 million years old, still forming at the ridge: no sunken continent.
found.evidence: Oldest Sediment Cored Above Basement: Depth: 104.5-149 meters Nature: Foram-bearing nannofossil ooze Age: Late Pliocene

features.label: Donnelly's 'Dolphin's Ridge' (Atlantis)
features.what: Donnelly drew the Atlantis of Plato as a land on the mid-Atlantic ridge next to the Azores, on a map in his book.

position.detail: Book map 'Map of Atlantis, with its islands and connecting ridges, from deep-sea soundings' (printed p. 47, scan page n64, 2174 x 3436 px). Control points: the map's own tick marks, longitude 50, 40, 30, 10 and 0 W (top and bottom, straight fit) and latitude 50 N to 40 S (ten ticks, Mercator fit). Outline traced from the drawn line and simplified to 20 vertices. The map's six Azores dots plot at about 24.2 W, 38.0 N in this grid, about 4 degrees east of the real islands, so the whole drawing is probably shifted by a similar amount. Fit residuals: 0.1 degree in longitude, up to 0.6 degree in latitude.

features.evidence: The Atlantis of Plato may have been confined to the " Dolphin Ridge " of our map.
features.notes: As drawn: about 2.85 million square km, about 3,000 km long and 1,600 km wide. Donnelly's text says an island 'one thousand miles in width, and two or three thousand miles long'. The outline is a schematic shape on a small map with no depth contour, so it is the shape he drew, not a measured shore.

features.label: 1898 cable-repair dredge (Termier)
features.what: Grappling irons dragged for a broken Brest to Cape Cod cable brought up chips of basalt glass (tachylyte) from rocky sea floor at about 3,100 m.
features.result: Termier read the glass as lava that cooled in air, so land that sank. Schuchert, Day and Pirsson replied that basalt glass forms under water too. The point lies on today's ridge axis, where new lava is erupted.

position.detail: Termier (Smithsonian Report 1915 translation, p. 226): 'north latitude 47 degrees 0 minutes and longitude 29 degrees 40 minutes west from Paris'. Converted to Greenwich by subtracting the Paris meridian (2 deg 20 min 14 s east of Greenwich): 27.33 W. Schuchert 1917 prints 29 deg 41 min. If the longitude were Greenwich, the point would be 29.67 W, about 177 km west, and 169 km from the ridge axis. Read as Paris, it lies 0.3 km from the PB2002 axis, which supports that reading.

features.evidence: It was in north latitude 47° 0' and longitude 29° 40' west from Paris, at a point about 500 miles north of the Azores. The mean depth was pretty nearly 1,700 fathoms, or 3,100 meters.
features.notes: Translation of Termier's 1912 lecture, read from an Internet Archive scan (OCR). The 1899 note to the Academie des Sciences was not read. GMRT gives 3,195 m at this point. The position is a ship's fix from 1898 with a grappling iron dragged for days, so the true dredge track is a line of unknown length.

features.label: DSDP Site 332 (Leg 37, 1974)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: Five holes in Deep Drill Valley, 30 km west of the ridge axis at 36.9 N, deepest hole 721.5 m, to test what the ridge crust is made of.
features.result: Late Pliocene ooze over basalt at 104 to 149 m: the sea floor here is only a few million years old and is basalt, not continent.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.what: foram-bearing nannofossil ooze with a few thin grey ash layers and pumice
column.age: Recent to late Pliocene (basement 3.0 Ma on the EarthByte age grid)

column.what: pillow and massive basalt with interlayered chalk, to the bottom of Hole 332B
column.age: crust formed at the ridge about 3 million years ago

features.evidence: Oldest Sediment Cored Above Basement: Depth: 104.5-149 meters Nature: Foram-bearing nannofossil ooze Age: Late Pliocene, near early-Pliocene-late Pliocene boundary
features.notes: Water depth 1,806 to 1,818 m. The site is 15.6 km from the PB2002 ridge axis. Basement depth is 104.5 to 149 m depending on the hole.

features.label: DSDP Site 333 (Leg 37, 1974)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: Two holes 1.8 km south-west of Site 332, at the foot of a fault scarp, to try deeper into the crust.
features.result: About 220 m of Recent to late Pliocene ooze over brecciated basalt: the same young ridge crust as Site 332.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.what: brecciated olivine-phyric basalt, soft sediment interbeds and rubble

features.evidence: About 220 meters of Recent to late Pliocene nanno-foram ooze overlie acoustic basement.
features.notes: Water depth 1,665.8 m. Hole 333A stuck at 529 m below the sea bed.

features.label: DSDP Site 334 (Leg 37, 1974)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: One hole on the flank of the ridge near magnetic anomaly 5, 376.5 m deep.
features.result: 260 m of ooze up to early late Miocene over basalt and gabbro: ocean crust about 10 million years old, with deep rocks pushed up near the surface.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.age: Recent to early late Miocene (grid age 9.9 Ma)
ocean crust about 10 million years old
deep ocean crust brought up by faulting

features.evidence: Acoustic basement lies beneath 259.5 meters of Recent to early late Miocene foram-bearing nannofossil ooze
features.notes: Water depth 2,619 m. Layer split of the basement (upper 50 m basalt, lower 67 m plutonic rock) is from the site summary; the depths 309.5 and 376.5 m are the lane's addition of those thicknesses to the 259.5 m basement top.

features.label: DSDP Site 335 (Leg 37, 1974)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: One hole 562 m deep farther west on the ridge flank.
features.result: 454 m of ooze, oldest about 13 million years, over pillow basalt: older crust farther from the ridge, always ocean-floor basalt.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.what: white to light grey foram-bearing nannofossil ooze (95 to 97 percent nannofossils)
column.age: Recent to middle Miocene, about 13 Ma at the base

column.what: uniform pillow basalt with glass rinds and chalk between pillows
column.age: ocean crust older than 13 Ma (grid age 16.7 Ma)

features.evidence: The oldest cored sediment is a foram-bearing nannofossil ooze which has been assigned to foraminiferal Zone N14 and nannoplankton Zone NN7, suggesting a middle Miocene age of approximately 13 m.y.
features.notes: Water depth 3,188 m.

features.label: DSDP Site 556 (Leg 82, 1981)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: Drilled on magnetic anomaly 12 on a flow line through the Azores triple junction, 639 m deep.
features.result: Latest early Oligocene sediment, 30 to 34 million years old, on basalt and gabbro: the plateau's west flank is old ocean floor.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.age: to latest early Oligocene at the base

column.what: basalt and basalt breccias, then gabbro and gabbro breccias
column.age: 30 to 34 Ma (nannofossils in breccias; grid age 29.6 Ma)

features.evidence: Nannofossils found in the basalt breccias at 10 m sub-basement are dated at 30 to 34 Ma in agreement with the magnetic anomaly age.
features.notes: Water depth 3,672 m. About 50 miles north of the Pico Fracture Zone.

features.label: DSDP Site 557 (Leg 82, 1981)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: Drilled on anomaly 5D in a broad elevated basin closer to the ridge; stopped by a storm after 3 m of basalt.
features.result: 460 m of sediment up to late Miocene over fresh basalt, on 18 million year old crust.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.what: sediment, volcaniclastic nannofossil chalk at the base (washed down)
column.age: to late Miocene at the base

column.what: fresh basalt, high in iron and titanium

features.evidence: Hole 557 (MAR-1) is located on Magnetic Anomaly 5D (18 Ma) in the center of a broad (40-km wide) elevated basin.
features.notes: Water depth 2,143 m, the shallowest Leg 82 site on the Azores side.

features.label: DSDP Site 558 (Leg 82, 1981)
features.who: Deep Sea Drilling Project shipboard scientific party
features.what: Drilled between anomalies 13 and 15, 561 m deep, cored through the whole sediment cover.
features.result: 408 m of Oligocene to Pleistocene ooze over basalt dated 34 to 37 million years: a calm, continuous ocean-floor record.

position.detail: Site data block of the site chapter, Initial Reports of the DSDP (position printed in degrees and minutes).

column.what: calcareous pelagic ooze and chalk, almost complete from lower Oligocene to Pleistocene
aphyric pillow basalts and breccias, then serpentinized gabbro

features.evidence: Nannofossils found within basalt breccias at the top of the basement are dated between 34 and 37 Ma, which is in agreement with the magnetic anomaly age.
features.notes: Water depth 3,754 m. A minor hiatus in the lower Pliocene.

features.label: Mid-Atlantic Ridge axis
features.what: The line where the North American plate pulls away from the Eurasian and African plates; new sea floor is made here.

position.detail: PB2002 plate boundaries, features NA-AF (30 N to the junction) and NA-EU (junction to 50.5 N), thinned to every second vertex.

features.evidence: 'Name': 'NA-EU', 'Source': 'by Peter Bird, 1999', 'PlateA': 'NA', 'PlateB': 'EU'
features.notes: The model's lines are coarse and simplified; they follow the ridge crest to within tens of km. The south part (NA-AF) is from Mueller and others (1987) as listed in the file.

features.label: Azores triple junction
features.what: Where the North American, Eurasian and African plates meet, just north-west of the islands; it is why the Azores are volcanic and quake-prone.

position.detail: Shared end vertex of NA-AF, NA-EU and EU-AF in PB2002_boundaries.json: [-29.7698, 39.3996]

features.notes: Published locations of the junction vary by tens of km because it is a broad zone.

features.label: Great Meteor Seamount
features.what: The largest seamount in the North Atlantic, a flat-topped volcano south of the plateau that people sometimes read as a drowned island.
features.result: Dredged basalts are 11 to 17 million years old and the sea floor under it is about 85 million years old; the flat top is 150 to 300 m under the sea.

position.detail: Wikidata Q3776136 P625; same value on the English Wikipedia page

features.evidence: Dredged basalts from the top of the eastern and southeastern flanks of the seamount have been K–Ar dated 10.7 ± 0.5 and 16.3 ± 0.4 million years old, respectively.
features.notes: Wikipedia is the only source I could open for the ages (the original GEOMAR and WHOI papers were behind bot checks). Heezen, Tharp and Ewing 1959 say the Atlantis, Plato, Cruiser and Great Meteor seamounts have 'broad, nearly flat summits at depths of 100-250 fathoms'. About 980 km from the Azores centre.

features.label: Azores Plateau (shallower than 1,829 m)
features.what: The raised area of sea floor around the islands, outlined where the sea is less than 1,000 fathoms (1,829 m) deep.
features.result: It is a swollen part of the volcanic ridge, about 116,000 square km in the GMRT grid, with a deep sea floor around it.

position.detail: GMRT GridServer, layer topo, bbox -40 to -18 E, 32 to 44 N, resolution low (about 3 km cells). The -1,829 m contour that encloses Sao Miguel and Terceira, traced by the lane and simplified to about 4 km. It joins the ridge crest north and south, so it runs to the edges of the clipped area in places.

features.evidence: The Azores Plateau is an area of 52,000 square miles of sea floor, surrounding the Azores Islands, where the depth is less than 1000 fathoms.
features.notes: Heezen and others give 52,000 square miles (134,700 square km); the lane's contour of this one box encloses 115,827 square km. The difference is the box edge and the lower-resolution grid.

features.label: Santa Maria at 58 m lower sea
features.what: The shore of Santa Maria if the sea stood 58 m lower, as it did about 11,600 years ago (about 9600 BCE).
features.result: The island would cover about 165 square km instead of 109, a wider rim of land on the same steep volcano, not a plain.

position.detail: GMRT GridServer, layer topo, bbox -31.5 to -24.5 E, 36.5 to 40 N, resolution med (cells 0.0044 x 0.0035 degrees, about 400 m). Contour of the grid at -58 m that encloses the island's Wikidata point, simplified to about 400 m.

features.evidence: GMRT grid, contour at 0 m around Santa Maria: 109 square km; at -58 m: 165 square km
features.notes: Lane's own computation, not a published map. It ignores that the islands have grown, eroded and moved up and down since 9600 BCE, and that the grid is a mix of ship soundings and predicted depth. The -58 m level is the lane world-9600bce's Barbados reading; other estimates are about -45 m.

measurements.evidence: If, however, the greater estimate of 210,000 square miles be taken, then the oceanic level would be reduced about 15 feet and this should show in a well marked terrace all along the Atlantic shores.

measurements.what: How fast global sea level rose from about 11,400 to 8,200 years ago
measurements.evidence: A period from ∼11.4–8.2 ka BP of near-uniform global rise. The average rate of rise during this 3.3 ka interval was ∼15 m⋅ka −1 with little convincing evidence of variations in this rate.

story.line: 1882: Donnelly draws Atlantis as 'Dolphin's Ridge', a mid-Atlantic land beside the Azores, from nineteenth-century soundings.
1898 to 1912: a cable repair drags up basalt glass 900 km north of the Azores. Termier says it proves recent sunken land.
1917: Schuchert, with Day and Pirsson, replies that basalt glass forms under water too, and the Azores are volcanic, not continental.
1931 and 1944: the ketch Atlantis cruises the Azores, and Pettersson argues continents do not sink and the ridge is building new crust.
1974: Leg 37 drills the ridge at 37 N. The crust is 3 to 16 million years old, basalt under 100 to 450 m of ooze.
1981: Leg 82 drills west of the Azores. The sea floor is 17 to 37 million years old: basalt and gabbro, never a continent.
The real plateau is a swollen volcanic ridge. At 9600 BCE sea level the islands would be only about a quarter bigger.

not_located.what: Termier's sunken region 'north of the Azores, and perhaps the very region of the Azores'
not_located.why: He gives no outline or area. Schuchert's sums (40,000 to 210,000 square miles) are his reading, not Termier's drawing.

not_located.what: Atlantis, Plato and Cruiser seamounts (the Great Meteor chain)
not_located.why: I could not open a source that prints their positions: the Geldmacher 2006 (GEOMAR) and Tucholke and Smoot 1990 (WHOI) PDFs sat behind bot checks. Heezen, Tharp and Ewing 1959 describe them (flat tops at 100 to 250 fathoms) but give no coordinates in the text.

not_located.what: Kolbe's freshwater diatoms in Albatross cores (Science 1957), cited by Malaise as signs of exposed ridge
not_located.why: The paper is paywalled and no open source gives the core positions. Sources found through search put the cores in the equatorial Atlantic, outside this scene.

not_located.what: Ewing's 1947 to 1949 'beach sand' cores from the ridge (Atlantis cruise 150)
not_located.why: I found only a search-result summary, no printed core positions and no readable copy of the National Geographic article or of Tolstoy and Ewing 1949.

not_located.what: Stations of the 1931 Woods Hole ketch Atlantis cruise around the Azores
not_located.why: The WHOI article gives no sounding or sampling positions and says the logbooks record no Atlantis finding.

not_located.what: The Swedish Deep-Sea Expedition (Albatross, 1947 to 1948) cores and track near the Azores
not_located.why: PANGAEA holds the expedition's tables (for example doi 10.1594/PANGAEA.858701) but they cover the whole world cruise and I did not map them.

not_located.what: Dolphin (1852 to 1853) and Challenger (1873 to 1876) soundings that Donnelly cites
not_located.why: Donnelly prints a frontispiece profile and one sounding map but no sounding table with positions in the chapter I read.

handoffs.what: Termier and Schuchert also discuss the Canary and Cape Verde islands as possible fragments of land.
Sea level at 9600 BCE: this lane uses -58 m (Barbados reading) and notes -45 m (global stack) from that lane's table.
Donnelly also cites Gorringe's 1875 bank of soundings 130 miles from Cape St Vincent (36 deg 29 min N, 11 deg 33 min W), a separate site.

not_verified: Ewing's beach-sand claim and its later explanation: not read at the source (see not_located).
Pettersson 1944 and Hogbom 1938 were not read; the account is Thorwald Franke's summary on atlantis-scout.de, a scholarly but individual site.
Termier's 1899 note to the Academie des Sciences about the tachylyte was not read. The 1915 Smithsonian translation and Schuchert's reprint of it were.
Schuchert 1917 was read from the Internet Archive scan of PNAS vol. 3 no. 2 (OCR), because the PNAS and PMC pages sit behind bot checks.

Age-grid, spreading-rate, depth and area figures marked 'lane' were computed by me from the GMRT and EarthByte 2020 files downloaded on 2026-11-11 (the local copies were later cleared). They are not published numbers.

The -58 m sea level for 9600 BCE comes from the world-9600bce lane's table (Abdul and others 2016 Barbados; Liu and Milliman 2004 via Wikipedia). I did not re-fetch those. Lambeck and others 2014 (fetched) gives rates but no level at 11.6 ka.

DSDP Leg 82 Sites 559 to 564 (33 to 35 N, 38 to 44 W) and Leg 94 were left out: they are on the ridge flank south or north of the Azores area. The NOAA Index to Marine and Lacustrine Geological Samples API address in the brief gave 404, so dredge and core positions from it were not searched.

Island ages (for example Santa Maria's oldest rocks) and the 'raised beach' claim in hypotheses.json were not fetched. Schuchert quotes Gagel 1910 for fossiliferous middle Miocene limestone inclusions in the Azores.
Great Meteor Seamount ages come from Wikipedia only.
Lourenco and others 1998 (Marine Geophysical Researches, new bathymetric compilation of the Azores Plateau) was not opened; Crossref holds no abstract.
